**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- **Affected part**: Whole plant (pseudostem + leaves)
- **Key features**:
  - Significant yellowing/chlorosis on the outer left leaf — outer leaves yellowing first is a hallmark of Panama Disease (Fusarium wilt)
  - Central/inner leaves appear stunted and crowded at the crown
  - **Dark brown discoloration at the pseudostem base** — characteristic vascular discoloration seen in Panama Disease
  - Overall plant wilt/decline

**Differential reasoning:**
- **Panama Disease**: Matches — progressive yellowing from outer leaves inward, vascular browning in pseudostem, plant wilting/collapse
- **Bunchy Top**: Would show stiff, upright, narrow leaves with dark streaks along margins; less pronounced yellowing
- **Yellow & Black Sigatoka**: Would show distinct yellow/black streaking on leaves without the vascular pseudostem symptoms
- **Cordana Leaf Spot**: Would show discrete oval/elongated spots with defined margins

The combination of outer-leaf chlorosis + pseudostem base discoloration + plant wilt strongly indicates Panama Disease.
